figurative_meaning_bn: যে দুষ্টদলকে কোনভাবে ধ্বংস করা যায় না
figurative_meaning_en: A wicked group or entity that cannot be destroyed by any means, regenerating endlessly
similar_in_english: Like the Hydra (cut off one head, two grow back)
example_sentences_in_bangla: এই দুর্নীতিগ্রস্ত দলটি রক্তবীজের বংশের মতো, কতবারই চেষ্টা করা হলো না ধ্বংস করতে।
শত্রুপক্ষের এই অংশ রক্তবীজের বংশের ন্যায় অবিনশ্বর।
example_sentences_in_english: This corrupt faction is like the lineage of Raktabija; no matter how many times we try, it can't be eradicated.
The enemy's this wing is as indestructible as Raktabija's progeny.
history: Derived from the Hindu mythological tale in Devi Mahatmya, where the demon Raktabija (blood-seed) multiplies from every drop of his blood spilled in battle, symbolizing an unbeatable evil force that only Goddess Durga could defeat by drinking his blood.
note: The idiom draws from Puranic lore, emphasizing futility against regenerating adversaries.
